row.평가 축: 에이전트(서빙 경험 기반 지속 학습, 진화하는 숨은 정책)
row.정의: 숨겨진 환경 정책이 시간에 따라 바뀌는 스트리밍 데이터셋(EESD) 형식의 벤치마크. 에이전트는 상호작용과 결과 피드백만으로 잠재 지식을 추론하고 적용하며 수정해야 한다. 리테일, 은행, 영업 피치 3개 도메인 9개 시나리오(난이도 L1~L3), 53개 환경 윈도우, 서빙 과제 4,508개와 보류 테스트 과제 3,210개(총 7,718개)로 구성된다. 윈도우마다 피드백이 제공되는 서빙 과제 뒤에 피드백 없는 테스트 과제가 온다. 리테일과 은행은 결정적 검증기로 이진 보상, 피치는 구조화 루브릭 점수(LLM 판정)로 채점한다. Hidden-Dependent와 Fully Specified 과제를 구분하며, 학습 없는 기준선 Blind와 숨은 정책을 알려주는 Oracle을 포함한다. 논문 결과는 논문 조건의 값이며 현재 전역 리더보드가 아니다.
row.대표 과제: 리테일 고객지원(주문 취소·변경, 반품·교환), 은행 사례 심사(카드 승인, 한도 증액, 이체 심사), 영업 피치 생성(제품 시트 기반 40~80단어 피치)
row.대표 예시·설명: 과제 설명: 에이전트가 사실 기반 제품 시트를 받아 짧은 영업 피치를 쓰고, 점수 피드백만으로 숨은 고객 선호 프로필을 추론해 이후 과제에 반영한다. 정책이 바뀌면 이전 지식을 수정해야 한다. 실제 시험 문항이 아니다.
row.이용 시 유의사항: 공식 저장소 README의 License 절과 LICENSE 파일이 저장소에 Apache-2.0을 부여하며, 과제 스트림과 환경 데이터(dataset/ 폴더)도 이 저장소에 포함되어 있다. Apache-2.0 조건(라이선스 사본 첨부, 변경 고지, 저작권·고지 유지)을 지켜야 한다. 공식 README에 lm-eval 언급이 없고 자체 명령줄 도구(slb)로 실행한다. 피치 도메인 채점에 LLM 판정 모델(논문은 GLM-5.3 Flash 사용)이 필요하다. 논문은 각 셀이 1회 실행 결과이며 표준오차를 제시하지 않고, Pitch L1은 효과적 속성 조합이 적어 문항 수를 독립 반복으로 해석하면 안 된다고 밝힌다. 하니스마다 실행 조건과 학습 계산량이 달라 하니스 효과만 분리한 비교가 아니다.

english_copy.axis: Agents (continual learning from serving experience in evolving hidden environments)
english_copy.definition: A benchmark built as evolving-environment streaming datasets (EESD) in which the governing policy is hidden and changes over time. An agent must infer, apply and revise latent knowledge from interaction and outcome feedback alone. It has nine scenarios (difficulty tiers L1-L3) across retail support, banking and sales-pitch generation, with 53 environment windows, 4,508 serving tasks and 3,210 held-out test tasks (7,718 in total). Each window has feedback-provided serving tasks followed by feedback-hidden test tasks. Retail and banking use deterministic verifiers with binary rewards; pitch uses a structured rubric score from an LLM judge. Tasks are split into Hidden-Dependent and Fully Specified, and non-learning Blind and Oracle baselines are included. Paper results hold under the paper's conditions and are not a current global leaderboard.
english_copy.task: Retail support (cancel or modify orders, return or exchange items), banking case review (card authorization, credit-limit increases, transfer screening), and sales-pitch generation (a 40-80 word pitch from a product sheet).
english_copy.example: Task description, not an actual test item: the agent receives a factual product sheet and writes a short sales pitch, then infers the hidden customer preference profile from score feedback alone and applies it to later tasks, revising it when the policy changes.

recommendations.metric: Hidden-case test reward (Adapt), 0-100 points: mean over the model's 45 lanes (five learning harnesses x nine scenario-difficulty settings, equal setting weight), Blind and Oracle excluded
recommendations.setting: Results reported in this paper (Table 3, Test (frozen state) Adapt column), not a current global leaderboard. Held-out test tasks of ServeLearnBench evaluated under the frozen learned state after the serving stream, Hidden-Dependent cases only; Retail and Banking are binary rewards scaled to 0-100 and Pitch is the 0-100 rubric rating. Unified high-effort regime, one attempt per scored item, 50 tool calls, 100-step runner guard, 256k output-token cap; each cell is one run. Each score averages across five different learning harnesses, so it is not a single-harness result.

screening.paper_title: ServeLearnBench: How Well Can Agents Self-Improve from Serving Experience?
screening.abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed to perform complex tasks in real-world environments. However, the knowledge required for correct behavior in these environments is often implicit, undisclosed, and subject to change over time. Recent continual-learning harnesses seek to address this challenge by enabling agents to improve from serving experience. Yet the effectiveness and limitations of these methods are not yet well characterized. Existing benchmarks provide only partial coverage: some explicitly provide the target knowledge, others assume a static environment, and those that support continual adaptation remain limited in scale and knowledge diversity. To enable systematic evaluation, we formalize an evolving-environment streaming dataset (EESD), in which agents must infer, apply, and revise latent environment knowledge from interaction and outcome feedback as hidden policies evolve, and introduce ServeLearnBench, spanning retail support, banking, and sales-pitch generation with 53 environment windows and 7,718 tasks. We evaluate five learning harnesses (RAG, Mem0, SkillOpt, Continual Harness, and Prime) across six models (GPT-5.6 Terra, Opus 5, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and GLM-5.3 Flash), covering 28 model-harness pairs and 252 learning runs. Our evaluation reveals three main findings: a substantial gap remains between task capability and learning from experience; continual adaptation is costly and can degrade already-correct behavior; and insufficient exploration emerges as a key bottleneck to effective adaptation. Overall, ServeLearnBench provides a controlled testbed for diagnosing these limitations and tracking progress toward agents that continually and reliably improve through serving experience.
